Question 1 · 9709/13/M/J/20 Q1
Find the set of values of m for which the line with equation y=mx+1 and the curve with equation
y=3x^2+2x+4
intersect at two distinct points. [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

At an intersection,
3x^2+2x+4=mx+1,
so
3x^2+(2-m)x+3=0.
For two distinct intersection points, this quadratic must have two distinct real roots:

(2-m)^2-4(3)(3)>0.

Hence

(2-m)^2>36
\Longleftrightarrow |2-m|>6.

Therefore
\boxed{m<-4\text{ or }m>8}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-13.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709-s20-ms-13.pdf.





Question 2 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q6(a–b)
The equation of a curve is y=2x^2+kx+k-1, where k is a constant.

Given that the line y=2x+3 is a tangent to the curve, find the value of k. [3]

It is now given that k=2.

Express the equation of the curve in the form y=2(x+a)^2+b, where a and b are constants, and hence state the coordinates of the vertex of the curve. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


At an intersection,

2x^2+kx+k-1=2x+3,
so
2x^2+(k-2)x+(k-4)=0.

Tangency means a repeated root, so the discriminant is zero:

(k-2)^2-4(2)(k-4)=0.

Thus
k^2-12k+36=(k-6)^2=0,

and \boxed{k=6}.

When k=2,

y=2x^2+2x+1=2\left(x^2+x+\frac14\right)=2\left(x+\frac12\right)^2.
Therefore a=\frac12, b=0, and the vertex is
\boxed{\left(-\frac12,0\right)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q6(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.





Question 3 · 9709/13/O/N/20 Q1(a–b)

Express x^2+6x+5 in the form (x+a)^2+b, where a and b are constants. [2]
The curve with equation y=x^2 is transformed to the curve with equation y=x^2+6x+5. Describe fully the transformation(s) involved. [2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


x^2+6x+5=x^2+6x+9-4=(x+3)^2-4.

So a=3, b=-4. The graph of y=x^2 is translated 3 units to the left and 4 units down:
\boxed{\text{translation by }\begin{pmatrix}-3\\-4\end{pmatrix}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_13.pdf, Q1(a–b), and matching 9709_w20_ms_13.pdf.





Question 4 · 9709/12/O/N/20 Q3
The equation of a curve is y=2x^2+m(2x+1), where m is a constant, and the equation of a line is y=6x+4.
Show that, for all values of (m), the line intersects the curve at two distinct points. [5]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Equating the two expressions for (y),
2x^2+m(2x+1)=6x+4,
which gives
2x^2+(2m-6)x+(m-4)=0.
Its discriminant is

\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(2m-6)^2-4(2)(m-4)\\
&=4m^2-32m+68\\
&=4\bigl((m-4)^2+1\bigr).
\end{aligned}

Since (m-4)^2+1>0 for every real m, \Delta>0 for every real m. Hence the quadratic has two distinct real roots, so the line intersects the curve at two distinct points for all m.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_12.pdf, Q3, and matching 9709_w20_ms_12.pdf.





Question 5 · 9709/12/F/M/21 Q2
By using a suitable substitution, solve the equation

(2x-3)^2-\frac{4}{(2x-3)^2}-3=0.

[4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Let
u=(2x-3)^2.
Then (u>0), and the equation becomes
u-\frac4u-3=0.
Multiplying by (u),
u^2-3u-4=0=(u-4)(u+1).
Because u>0, reject u=-1, so u=4. Therefore

(2x-3)^2=4
\Longrightarrow 2x-3=\pm2.

Hence
\boxed{x=\frac12\text{ or }x=\frac52}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_12.pdf, Q2, and matching 9709_m21_ms_12.pdf.





Question 6 · 9709/12/F/M/21 Q4
A line has equation y=3x+k and a curve has equation y=x^2+kx+6, where k is a constant.
Find the set of values of (k) for which the line and curve have two distinct points of intersection. [5]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

At an intersection,
x^2+kx+6=3x+k,
so
x^2+(k-3)x+(6-k)=0.
For two distinct intersections,

\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(k-3)^2-4(6-k)>0\\
&=k^2-2k-15>0\\
&=(k-5)(k+3)>0.
\end{aligned}

Therefore
\boxed{k<-3\text{ or }k>5}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_12.pdf, Q4, and matching 9709_m21_ms_12.pdf.





Question 7 · 9709/13/M/J/21 Q3
A line with equation y=mx-6 is a tangent to the curve with equation y=x^2-4x+3.
Find the possible values of the constant (m), and the corresponding coordinates of the points at which the line touches the curve. [6]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

At a point of contact,
x^2-4x+3=mx-6,
so
x^2-(m+4)x+9=0.
For tangency,

(m+4)^2-4(1)(9)=0.

Thus m+4=\pm6, giving
m=2\quad\text{or}\quad m=-10.

The repeated root is x=(m+4)/2. For m=2, x=3 and y=2(3)-6=0, giving (3,0). For m=-10, x=-3 and y=-10(-3)-6=24, giving (-3,24).
\boxed{(m,x,y)=(2,3,0)\text{ or }(-10,-3,24)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_13.pdf, Q3, and matching 9709_s21_ms_13.pdf.





Question 8 · 9709/11/M/J/21 Q6
The equation of a curve is y=(2k-3)x^2-kx-(k-2), where k is a constant. The line y=3x-4 is a tangent to the curve.
Find the value of (k). [5]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Equating the curve and the line,

(2k-3)x^2-kx-(k-2)=3x-4,

so

(2k-3)x^2-(k+3)x-(k-6)=0.

Tangency requires the discriminant to be zero:

(k+3)^2+4(2k-3)(k-6)=0.

Expanding,
k^2+6k+9+8k^2-60k+72=0,
so
9k^2-54k+81=9(k-3)^2=0.

Therefore \boxed{k=3}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_11.pdf, Q6, and matching 9709_s21_ms_11.pdf.





Question 9 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q2
A curve has equation y=x^2+2cx+4 and a straight line has equation y=4x+c, where c is a constant.
Find the set of values of (c) for which the curve and line intersect at two distinct points. [5]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Equating the two equations,
x^2+2cx+4=4x+c,
so
x^2+(2c-4)x+(4-c)=0.
For two distinct intersections,

\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(2c-4)^2-4(4-c)>0\\
&=4c^2-12c\\
&=4c(c-3)>0.
\end{aligned}

Hence
\boxed{c<0\text{ or }c>3}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf, Q2, and matching 9709_m22_ms_12.pdf.





Question 10 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q5(a–b)

Express 2x^2-8x+14 in the form 2(x-a)^2+b. [2]

The functions f and g are defined by f(x)=x^2 and g(x)=2x^2-8x+14, for x\in\mathbb R.

Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of y=f(x) onto the graph of y=g(x), making clear the order in which the transformations are applied. [4]



Show detailed mark scheme answer





2x^2-8x+14=2(x^2-4x+4)+6=2(x-2)^2+6.

So a=2, b=6.

Starting from y=x^2, first apply a stretch parallel to the y-axis with scale factor 2:

y=2x^2.

Then translate 2 units to the right and 6 units upwards:
y=2(x-2)^2+6.

Thus the required sequence is \boxed{\text{vertical stretch factor }2,\text{ followed by translation }(2,6)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching 9709_m22_ms_12.pdf.





Question 11 · 9709/12/O/N/22 Q3(a–b)

Find the set of values of k for which the equation 8x^2+kx+2=0 has no real roots. [2]
Solve the equation 8\cos^2\theta-10\cos\theta+2=0 for 0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


No real roots means \Delta<0:

k^2-4(8)(2)<0\Longleftrightarrow k^2-64<0.
Therefore \boxed{-8<k<8}.

Let u=\cos\theta. Then

8u^2-10u+2=0\Longleftrightarrow 4u^2-5u+1=0,
so

(4u-1)(u-1)=0.

Hence \cos\theta=\frac14 or \cos\theta=1. In the stated interval,
\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac14\right)=75.5^\circ\quad\text{or}\quad\theta=0^\circ.

Thus \boxed{\theta=0^\circ,\ 75.5^\circ} (to 1 decimal place for the non-exact angle).

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching 9709_w22_ms_12.pdf.





Question 12 · 9709/11/M/J/22 Q1(a–b)

Express x^2-8x+11 in the form (x+p)^2+q, where p and q are constants. [2]
Hence find the exact solutions of the equation x^2-8x+11=1. [2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer




x^2-8x+11=x^2-8x+16-5=(x-4)^2-5.
Thus p=-4, q=-5.




(x-4)^2-5=1
\Longrightarrow (x-4)^2=6.

Therefore
\boxed{x=4\pm\sqrt6}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_11.pdf, Q1(a–b), and matching 9709_s22_ms_11.pdf.





Question 13 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q1
A line has equation y=3x-2k and a curve has equation y=x^2-kx+2, where k is a constant.
Show that the line and the curve meet for all values of (k). [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

At an intersection,
x^2-kx+2=3x-2k,
so
x^2-(k+3)x+(2+2k)=0.
Its discriminant is

\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(k+3)^2-4(2+2k)\\
&=k^2-2k+1\\
&=(k-1)^2\ge0.
\end{aligned}

Thus there are real values of x for every real k, so the line and curve meet for all values of k. When k=1, \Delta=0 and the intersection is a repeated point; for all other k, \Delta>0.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_m23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 14 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q4
Solve the equation
8x^6+215x^3-27=0.
[3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Let u=x^3. Then
8u^2+215u-27=0.
The discriminant is 215^2+4(8)(27)=217^2, so

u=\frac{-215\pm217}{16}.

Hence u=\frac18 or u=-27. Returning to x,
x^3=\frac18\Longrightarrow x=\frac12,
\qquad x^3=-27\Longrightarrow x=-3.

Therefore \boxed{x=\frac12\text{ or }x=-3}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf, Q4, and matching 9709_m23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 15 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q3(a–b)

Express 4x^2-24x+p in the form a(x+b)^2+c, where a and b are integers and c is to be given in terms of the constant p. [2]
Hence or otherwise find the set of values of p for which the equation 4x^2-24x+p=0 has no real roots. [1]



Show detailed mark scheme answer





4x^2-24x+p=4(x^2-6x+9)+p-36=4(x-3)^2+p-36.

Thus a=4, b=-3, c=p-36.

Since 4(x-3)^2\ge0, the minimum value of the quadratic is p-36. For no real roots, this minimum must be positive:

p-36>0.

Therefore \boxed{p>36}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 16 · 9709/12/O/N/23 Q6(a–c)
The equation of a curve is y=x^2-8x+5.

Find the coordinates of the minimum point of the curve. [2]

The curve is stretched by a factor of 2 parallel to the (y)-axis and then translated by
\begin{pmatrix}4\\1\end{pmatrix}.

Find the coordinates of the minimum point of the transformed curve. [2]
Find the equation of the transformed curve. Give the answer in the form y=ax^2+bx+c, where a, b and c are integers to be found. [4]



Show detailed mark scheme answer




y=x^2-8x+5=(x-4)^2-11,
so the minimum point is \boxed{(4,-11)}.

A vertical stretch by factor 2 sends the minimum value -11 to -22. The subsequent translation by (4,1) sends the vertex (4,-22) to

\boxed{(8,-21)}.

After the vertical stretch,

y=2(x-4)^2-22.

Translating by (4,1) replaces x by x-4 and adds 1 to y:

$y=2((x-4)-4)^2-22+1=2(x-8)^2-21$.

Expanding,
\boxed{y=2x^2-32x+107}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf, Q6(a–c), and matching 9709_w23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 17 · 9709/11/M/J/24 Q1(a–b)

Express 3y^2-12y-15 in the form 3(y+a)^2+b, where a and b are constants. [2]
Hence find the exact solutions of the equation 3x^4-12x^2-15=0. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer





3y^2-12y-15=3(y^2-4y-5)=3\bigl((y-2)^2-9\bigr),

so
\boxed{3y^2-12y-15=3(y-2)^2-27}.

Thus a=-2, b=-27.

Put y=x^2 in the completed-square result:


3(x^2-2)^2-27=0
\Longrightarrow (x^2-2)^2=9.

Therefore x^2-2=\pm3. This gives x^2=5 or x^2=-1. Only the first gives real solutions, so
\boxed{x=\pm\sqrt5}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q1(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf.





Question 18 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q11
The function (f) is defined by
f(x)=10+6x-x^2\quad\text{for }x\in\mathbb R.
By completing the square, find the range of (f). [3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer


f(x)=10+6x-x^2=-(x^2-6x-10)
=-(x-3)^2+19.

Since -(x-3)^2\le0, the greatest value of f is 19, attained at x=3. As x\to\pm\infty, f(x)\to-\infty. Hence
\boxed{\text{range of }f=(-\infty,19]}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q11, and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.





Question 19 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q11(a–b)
The function (f) is defined by
f(x)=3+6x-2x^2\quad\text{for }x\in\mathbb R.
Express f(x) in the form a-b(x-c)^2, where a, b and c are constants, and state the range of f. [3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer


f(x)=3+6x-2x^2=-2(x^2-3x)+3


=-2\left((x-\tfrac32)^2-\tfrac94\right)+3
=-2\left(x-\tfrac32\right)^2+\frac{15}{2}.

Thus a=\frac{15}{2}, b=2, c=\frac32. The maximum value is \frac{15}{2}, and the quadratic decreases without bound, so
\boxed{\text{range of }f=(-\infty,\tfrac{15}{2}]}.

Reflecting in the x-axis gives


y=2\left(x-\frac32\right)^2-\frac{15}{2},

whose minimum is at (3/2,-15/2). Translating upwards by 15/2 gives

\boxed{h(x)=2\left(x-\frac32\right)^2},

with minimum point at the origin.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q11(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.





Question 20 · 9709/12/O/N/24 Q7(a–b)
By expressing -2x^2+8x+11 in the form -a(x-b)^2+c, where a, b and c are positive integers, find the coordinates of the vertex of the graph with equation y=-2x^2+8x+11. [3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer


\begin{aligned}
y&=-2(x^2-4x)+11\\
&=-2\bigl((x-2)^2-4\bigr)+11\\
&=-2(x-2)^2+19.
\end{aligned}

Thus a=2, b=2, c=19. Since the coefficient of the square is negative, the graph has a maximum (its vertex) at
\boxed{(2,19)}.

The intersections with the line satisfy


-2x^2+8x+11=8x+9
\Longrightarrow x=\pm1.

Between these points the parabola is above the line, so the shaded area is

\begin{aligned}
A&=\int_{-1}^{1}\left[(-2x^2+8x+11)-(8x+9)\right]dx\\
&=\int_{-1}^{1}(2-2x^2)\,dx
=\boxed{\frac83}.
\end{aligned}


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf.

title: 1.1 Quadratics
text:
3. Quick checklist


能从 quadratic curve 与 line 的交点方程写出 (a,b,c)
能根据题目要求选用 \Delta>0、\Delta=0 或 \Delta<0
能把二次式写成 completed-square form，并读出 vertex、maximum/minimum 与 range
能解 quadratic inequality 并正确写出 interval notation
能用 u=x^2、u=x^3 或 u=(2x-3)^2 降次，再回代原变量

title: 1.3 Coordinate geometry
text:
重要本节考纲要求



本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.3 Coordinate geometry：

使用 y=mx+c、y-y_1=m(x-x_1)、ax+by+c=0 等直线形式；
计算 gradient、distance、midpoint，并判断 parallel/perpendicular；
理解 (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2 及 expanded circle equation；
用 algebraic methods 处理 lines and circles，包括 tangent perpendicular to radius、angle in a semicircle 和 symmetry；
用交点的代数方程理解 graph 与 equation 的关系。

下列 20 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干只把 PDF 排版符号整理为 LaTeX，没有改写或编造题目；答案按对应 mark scheme 的步骤展开。题目中的必要图形均从原始 PDF 独立提取为 SVG，不使用整页截图。

title: 1.3 Coordinate geometry
text:
1. Core knowledge

Lines and gradients
两点 (x_1,y_1)、(x_2,y_2) 的 gradient 是
m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}.
因此：

\text{parallel}\Longleftrightarrow m_1=m_2,
\qquad
\text{perpendicular}\Longleftrightarrow m_1m_2=-1.

过 (x_1,y_1) 且 gradient 为 m 的直线写成
y-y_1=m(x-x_1).
Vertical line 要单独写成 x=a，不能强行写成 y=mx+c。


Circles
标准式

(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2

的 centre 是 (a,b)，radius 是 r。一般式
x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0
可通过 completing the square 化为标准式。圆上点 P 处的 tangent 与 radius CP perpendicular；因此先求 centre，再用 perpendicular gradient 或点到直线距离，通常是最稳妥的方法。


Intersections and tangency
求 line 与 circle 的交点时，把 line equation 代入 circle equation，得到关于 x 或 y 的 quadratic。两 distinct intersections 对应 two distinct real roots；tangent 对应 repeated root，也就是 discriminant 为 0。
若圆心为 C，直线为 ax+by+c=0，圆心到直线的距离为

d=\frac{|a x_C+b y_C+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}.

当直线是 tangent 时，d=r。


Perpendicular bisector and circle geometry
线段 AB 的 perpendicular bisector：

求 midpoint M；
求 AB 的 gradient；
取 perpendicular gradient；
写出经过 (M) 的直线。

圆的 diameter 的 midpoint 是 centre；若 AB 是 diameter，则 centre 是 AB 的 midpoint，radius 是 AB/2。


Coordinate formula toolkit
两点 A(x_1,y_1)、B(x_2,y_2) 之间的 distance 与 midpoint 为

AB=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2},qquad
M=\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2},\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right).

直线可以写成 y=mx+c、y-y_1=m(x-x_1) 或 ax+by+c=0。Vertical line 必须写成 x=k；parallel lines 有相同 gradient，perpendicular lines 满足 m_1m_2=-1。


Circle methods
标准圆方程

(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2

的 centre 是 (a,b)，radius 是 r。一般式
x^2+y^2+2fx+2gy+c=0
要分别对 x、y completing the square。若直线与圆相交，把直线代入圆方程；two intersections、tangent 和 no intersection 分别对应 quadratic 的 \Delta>0、\Delta=0 和 \Delta<0。
圆上点的 tangent perpendicular to the radius。求 tangent 时可先求 radius gradient，再取 negative reciprocal；也可以使用 centre 到直线的 perpendicular distance 等于 r。

title: 1.3 Coordinate geometry
text:
2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions


Question 1 · 9709/11/O/N/20 Q5(a–b)
The equation of a line is y=mx+c, where m and c are constants, and the equation of a curve is xy=16.

Given that the line is a tangent to the curve, express m in terms of c. [3]
Given instead that m=-4, find the set of values of c for which the line intersects the curve at two distinct points. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

The curve can be written as y=16/x. At an intersection with y=mx+c,
x(mx+c)=16,
so
mx^2+cx-16=0.


Tangency means a repeated root, so

c^2-4(m)(-16)=0\Longrightarrow c^2+64m=0.
Hence
\boxed{m=-\frac{c^2}{64}}.


With m=-4,

-4x^2+cx-16=0,
or equivalently 4x^2-cx+16=0. For two distinct points,
c^2-4(4)(16)>0\Longrightarrow c^2>256.
Therefore
\boxed{c<-16\text{ or }c>16}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_11.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching 9709_w20_ms_11.pdf.





Question 2 · 9709/11/O/N/20 Q10(a–c)
The coordinates of the points A and B are (-1,-2) and (7,4) respectively.

Find the equation of the circle C, for which AB is a diameter. [4]
Find the equation of the tangent T to circle C at the point B. [4]
Find the equation of the circle which is the reflection of circle C in the line T. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


The midpoint of (AB) is

C=\left(\frac{-1+7}{2},\frac{-2+4}{2}\right)=(3,1).
Also,
AB^2=(7+1)^2+(4+2)^2=8^2+6^2=100,
so the radius is (5). Therefore
\boxed{(x-3)^2+(y-1)^2=25}.


The radius CB has gradient \frac68=\frac34. The tangent gradient is -\frac43, so

y-4=-\frac43(x-7).
Hence
\boxed{4x+3y=40}.


Reflect the centre C=(3,1) in 4x+3y-40=0. The perpendicular distance calculation gives the reflected centre

C'=(11,7).
Reflection preserves the radius, so the reflected circle is
\boxed{(x-11)^2+(y-7)^2=25}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_11.pdf, Q10(a–c), and matching 9709_w20_ms_11.pdf.





Question 3 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q11(a–d)
The equation of a circle with centre (C) is
x^2+y^2-8x+4y-5=0.

Find the radius of the circle and the coordinates of (C). [3]

The point (P(1,2)) lies on the circle.

Show that the equation of the tangent to the circle at P is 4y=3x+5. [3]

The point (Q) also lies on the circle and (PQ) is parallel to the (x)-axis.

Write down the coordinates of (Q). [2]

The tangents to the circle at (P) and (Q) meet at (T).

Find the coordinates of (T). [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer




x^2-8x+y^2+4y-5=0
\Longrightarrow (x-4)^2+(y+2)^2=25.

Thus \boxed{C=(4,-2)} and \boxed{r=5}.

The radius CP has vector (-3,4), so its gradient is -\frac43. The tangent gradient is \frac34. Through P=(1,2),

y-2=\frac34(x-1)\Longrightarrow \boxed{4y=3x+5}.


Since PQ is horizontal, y_Q=2. Substitution into the circle gives


(x-4)^2+16=25\Longrightarrow x-4=\pm3.

The point different from P is \boxed{Q=(7,2)}.

The tangent at (Q) has gradient (-3/4), so

y-2=-\frac34(x-7)\Longrightarrow 3x+4y=29.

Together with 4y=3x+5,
6x=34\Longrightarrow x=\frac{17}{3},\qquad y=\frac{11}{2}.

Therefore \boxed{T=(17/3,11/2)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q11(a–d), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.





Question 4 · 9709/13/M/J/20 Q10(a–b)
The coordinates of two points A and B are (-7,3) and (5,11) respectively.

Show that the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB is 3x+2y=11. [4]
A circle passes through A and B and its centre lies on the line 12x-5y=70. Find an equation of the circle. [5]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


The midpoint is

M=\left(\frac{-7+5}{2},\frac{3+11}{2}\right)=(-1,7).
The gradient of AB is \frac8{12}=\frac23, so the perpendicular gradient is -\frac32. Hence
y-7=-\frac32(x+1)\Longrightarrow \boxed{3x+2y=11}.


The centre lies on both 3x+2y=11 and 12x-5y=70. Solving,

\boxed{C=(5,-2)}.

The radius squared using (A) is
r^2=(5+7)^2+(-2-3)^2=144+25=169.
Therefore
\boxed{(x-5)^2+(y+2)^2=169}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-13.pdf, Q10(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-13.pdf.





Question 5 · 9709/12/F/M/21 Q8(a–b)
The points A=(7,1), B=(7,9) and C=(1,9) are on the circumference of a circle.

Find an equation of the circle. [5]
Find an equation of the tangent to the circle at (B). [2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

Since AB is vertical, its perpendicular bisector is y=5. Since BC is horizontal, its perpendicular bisector is x=4. Thus the centre is O=(4,5).
The radius squared is
r^2=(7-4)^2+(1-5)^2=9+16=25.
Therefore
\boxed{(x-4)^2+(y-5)^2=25}.

At (B), the radius has gradient (4/3), so the tangent gradient is (-3/4). Hence
y-9=-\frac34(x-7),
or
\boxed{3x+4y=57}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_12.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching 9709_m21_ms_12.pdf.





Question 6 · 9709/11/M/J/21 Q10(a–b)
The equation of a circle is
x^2+y^2-4x+6y-77=0.

Find the x-coordinates of the points A and B where the circle intersects the x-axis. [2]
Find the point of intersection of the tangents to the circle at (A) and (B). [6]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


On the x-axis, y=0:

x^2-4x-77=0=(x-11)(x+7).

Thus the points are (-7,0) and (11,0), so the x-coordinates are \boxed{-7,11}.

Complete the square:


(x-2)^2+(y+3)^2=90,

so the centre is (2,-3). At (-7,0), the radius gradient is -1/3, so the tangent is y=3x+21. At (11,0), the radius gradient is 1/3, so the tangent is y=-3x+33.
Solving,
3x+21=-3x+33\Longrightarrow x=2,qquad y=27.

Therefore the tangents meet at \boxed{(2,27)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_11.pdf, Q10(a–b), and matching 9709_s21_ms_11.pdf.





Question 7 · 9709/12/O/N/21 Q6
Points A and B have coordinates (8,3) and (p,q) respectively. The equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB is y=-2x+4.
Find the values of (p) and (q). [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

The perpendicular bisector has gradient -2, so AB has gradient 1/2:
\frac{q-3}{p-8}=\frac12\Longrightarrow p=2q+2.
The midpoint \left(\frac{8+p}{2},\frac{3+q}{2}\right) lies on y=-2x+4:
\frac{3+q}{2}=-2\left(\frac{8+p}{2}\right)+4=-4-p.

Hence 2p+q=-11. Combining with p=2q+2,
q=-3,qquad p=-4.

Therefore \boxed{p=-4,\ q=-3}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_12.pdf, Q6, and matching 9709_s21_ms_12.pdf.





Question 8 · 9709/11/O/N/21 Q7(a–b)
A circle with centre (5,2) passes through the point (7,5).

Find an equation of the circle. [2]

The line y=5x-10 intersects the circle at A and B.

Find the exact length of the chord AB. [7]



Show detailed mark scheme answer




r^2=(7-5)^2+(5-2)^2=13,
so
\boxed{(x-5)^2+(y-2)^2=13}.


Substitute y=5x-10:


(x-5)^2+(5x-12)^2=13.

This simplifies to
26x^2-130x+156=0
\Longrightarrow (x-2)(x-3)=0.

The intersection points are (2,0) and (3,5). Thus
AB=\sqrt{(3-2)^2+(5-0)^2}=\boxed{\sqrt{26}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w21_ms_11.pdf.





Question 9 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q6(a–b)



Original extracted diagram for Question 9


The circle with equation (x+1)^2+(y-2)^2=85 and the straight line with equation y=3x-20 are shown in the diagram. The line intersects the circle at A and B, and the centre of the circle is at C.

Find, by calculation, the coordinates of A and B. [4]
Find an equation of the circle which has its centre at C and for which the line with equation y=3x-20 is a tangent to the circle. [4]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


Substitute y=3x-20:


(x+1)^2+(3x-22)^2=85
\Longrightarrow 10x^2-130x+400=0.

Thus
x^2-13x+40=0=(x-5)(x-8).

The corresponding y-coordinates are -5 and 4. Hence the two points are
\boxed{(5,-5)\text{ and }(8,4)}.


The centre is C=(-1,2). The distance from C to 3x-y-20=0 is


r=\frac{|3(-1)-2-20|}{\sqrt{3^2+(-1)^2}}=\frac{25}{\sqrt{10}}.

Therefore the required circle is
\boxed{(x+1)^2+(y-2)^2=\frac{125}{2}}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf, Q6(a–b), and matching 9709_m22_ms_12.pdf. The diagram is an independently extracted, annotation-cleaned SVG from the original PDF.





Question 10 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q8(a–b)



Original extracted diagram for Question 10


The diagram shows the circle with equation (x-2)^2+y^2=8. The chord AB of the circle intersects the positive y-axis at A and is parallel to the x-axis.

Find, by calculation, the coordinates of A and B. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

Since A is on the positive y-axis, x=0. Hence
(-2)^2+y^2=8\Longrightarrow y^2=4,
so A=(0,2). Because AB is parallel to the x-axis, y_B=2. Then

(x_B-2)^2+2^2=8\Longrightarrow (x_B-2)^2=4.

The point other than A has x_B=4, so
\boxed{A=(0,2),\quad B=(4,2)}.


The shaded segment is between the circle and the chord AB, and is rotated about the x-axis. Since the circle is


y^2=8-(x-2)^2,

the volume is

\begin{aligned}
V&=\pi\int_0^4\left(8-(x-2)^2-2^2\right)dx\\
&=\pi\int_0^4\left(4-(x-2)^2\right)dx
=\boxed{\frac{32\pi}{3}}.
\end{aligned}


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching 9709_m22_ms_12.pdf. The diagram is an independently extracted, annotation-cleaned SVG from the original PDF.





Question 11 · 9709/11/M/J/22 Q9(a–b)
The equation of a circle is
x^2+y^2+6x-2y-26=0.

Find the coordinates of the centre of the circle and the radius. Hence find the coordinates of the lowest point on the circle. [4]
Find the set of values of the constant k for which the line y=kx-5 intersects the circle at two distinct points. [6]



Show detailed mark scheme answer





(x+3)^2+(y-1)^2=36.

Thus the centre is (-3,1), radius 6, and the lowest point is
\boxed{(-3,-5)}.


Substitute y=kx-5:


(1+k^2)x^2+(6-12k)x+9=0.

For two distinct intersections,

\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(6-12k)^2-36(1+k^2)>0\\
&=36(3k^2-4k)>0\\
&=36k(3k-4)>0.
\end{aligned}

Hence
\boxed{k<0\text{ or }k>\frac43}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_s22_qp_11.pdf, Q9(a–b), and matching 9709_s22_ms_11.pdf.





Question 12 · 9709/11/O/N/22 Q11(a–c)



Original extracted diagram for Question 12


The diagram shows the circle with equation x^2+y^2=20. Tangents touching the circle at points B and C pass through A=(0,10).

By letting the equation of a tangent be y=mx+10, find the two possible values of m. [4]
Find the coordinates of B and C. [3]

The point (D) is where the circle crosses the positive (x)-axis.

Find angle (BDC) in degrees. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


Substitute y=mx+10 into x^2+y^2=20:


(1+m^2)x^2+20mx+80=0.

Tangency gives

(20m)^2-4(1+m^2)(80)=0
\Longrightarrow m^2=4.

Thus \boxed{m=2\text{ or }m=-2}.

The repeated root is x=-20m/[2(1+m^2)]=-2m. Therefore the points of contact are

\boxed{B=(-4,2),\quad C=(4,2)}
in either order.

D=(2\sqrt5,0). Using vectors \overrightarrow{DB} and \overrightarrow{DC},

\cos\angle BDC=\frac{\overrightarrow{DB}\cdot\overrightarrow{DC}}{|DB||DC|}=\frac1{\sqrt5}.

Hence
\boxed{\angle BDC=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac1{\sqrt5}\right)=63.4^\circ}
to 1 decimal place.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_11.pdf, Q11(a–c), and matching 9709_w22_ms_11.pdf. The diagram is an independently extracted SVG from the original PDF.





Question 13 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q5
Points A=(7,12) and B lie on a circle with centre (-2,5). The line AB has equation y=-2x+26.
Find the coordinates of (B). [6]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

The radius through (A) has squared length
r^2=(7+2)^2+(12-5)^2=9^2+7^2=130.
Any point B=(x,-2x+26) on the circle satisfies

(x+2)^2+(-2x+21)^2=130.

Expanding and simplifying,
5x^2-80x+315=0
\Longrightarrow (x-7)(x-9)=0.

The root x=7 gives the known point A. Thus x_B=9, and
y_B=-2(9)+26=8.

Therefore \boxed{B=(9,8)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf, Q5, and matching 9709_m23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 14 · 9709/13/O/N/23 Q2(a–b)
The circle with equation (x-3)^2+(y-5)^2=40 intersects the y-axis at points A and B.

Find the y-coordinates of A and B, expressing your answers in terms of surds. [2]
Find the equation of the circle which has AB as its diameter. [2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

On the y-axis, x=0:
9+(y-5)^2=40\Longrightarrow (y-5)^2=31.
Thus the y-coordinates are \boxed{5+\sqrt{31}\text{ and }5-\sqrt{31}}.
The midpoint of A and B is (0,5), and their distance is 2\sqrt{31}, so the circle with AB as diameter has centre (0,5) and radius \sqrt{31}:
\boxed{x^2+(y-5)^2=31}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_13.pdf, Q2(a–b), and matching 9709_w23_ms_13.pdf.





Question 15 · 9709/11/O/N/23 Q11(a–c)



Original extracted diagram for Question 15


The diagram shows the circle (x-4)^2+(y+1)^2=40. Parallel tangents, each with gradient 1, touch the circle at points A and B.

Find the equation of the line AB, giving the answer in the form y=mx+c. [3]
Find the coordinates of (A), giving each coordinate in surd form. [4]
Find the equation of the tangent at A, giving the answer in the form y=mx+c, where c is in surd form. [2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


The centre is (4,-1). A line of gradient 1 has form y=x+c. The distance from the centre to x-y+c=0 must be 2\sqrt{10}:

\frac{|4-(-1)+c|}{\sqrt2}=2\sqrt{10}\Longrightarrow |5+c|=2\sqrt5.

The line joining the two contact points is perpendicular to the parallel tangents, so it has gradient -1 and passes through the centre (4,-1). Hence
\boxed{AB:y=-x+3}.


The radius CA is perpendicular to AB, so its gradient is -1. The perpendicular through C is y=-x+3. Intersecting with the upper tangent,

-x+3=x-5+2\sqrt5
\Longrightarrow x=4-\sqrt5,

and
y=\sqrt5-1.

Therefore \boxed{A=(4-\sqrt5,\sqrt5-1)}.

The radius gradient is (-1), so the tangent gradient is (1). Thus the tangent at (A) is the upper parallel tangent:

\boxed{y=x-5+2\sqrt5}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_11.pdf, Q11(a–c), and matching 9709_w23_ms_11.pdf. The diagram is an independently extracted SVG from the original PDF.





Question 16 · 9709/12/O/N/23 Q11(a–c)
The coordinates of points A, B and C are (6,4), (p,7) and (14,18) respectively, where p is a constant. The line AB is perpendicular to the line BC.

Given that p<10, find the value of p. [4]

A circle passes through the points (A), (B) and (C).

Find the equation of the circle. [3]
Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at C, giving the answer in the form dx+ey+f=0. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


The perpendicular condition gives

\frac{3}{p-6}\cdot\frac{11}{14-p}=-1.

Therefore

(p-6)(14-p)=-33
\Longrightarrow p^2-20p+51=0.

So p=3 or 17. Since p<10, \boxed{p=3}, hence B=(3,7).

Let the circle be x^2+y^2+Dx+Ey+F=0. Substitution of A, B, C gives


6D+4E+F=-52,
 
3D+7E+F=-58,
 
14D+18E+F=-520.

Solving gives D=-20, E=-22, F=156. Hence
\boxed{x^2+y^2-20x-22y+156=0}.


The centre is (10,11), so the radius C=(14,18) has gradient 7/4. The tangent gradient is -4/7. Thus

y-18=-\frac47(x-14),
which simplifies to
\boxed{4x+7y-182=0}.


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf, Q11(a–c), and matching 9709_w23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 17 · 9709/11/M/J/24 Q10
The equation of a circle is (x-3)^2+y^2=18. The line with equation y=mx+c passes through the point (0,-9) and is a tangent to the circle.
Find the two possible values of m and, for each value of m, find the coordinates of the point at which the tangent touches the circle. [8]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Since the line passes through (0,-9), it is y=mx-9, or mx-y-9=0. The centre is (3,0) and the radius is 3\sqrt2. Tangency gives

\frac{|3m-9|}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}=3\sqrt2.

Squaring and simplifying,

(m-3)^2=2(m^2+1)
\Longrightarrow m^2+6m-7=0.

Thus \boxed{m=1\text{ or }m=-7}.
For m=1, the line is x-y-9=0. The perpendicular foot from (3,0) is \boxed{(6,-3)}.
For m=-7, the line is 7x+y+9=0. The perpendicular foot from (3,0) is \boxed{\left(-\frac65,-\frac35\right)}.
Both points lie on (x-3)^2+y^2=18, confirming the tangent points.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q10, and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p11.pdf.





Question 18 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q7(a–b)
The equation of a circle is (x-6)^2+(y+a)^2=18. The line with equation y=2a-x is a tangent to the circle.

Find the two possible values of the constant a. [5]
For the greater value of a, find the equation of the diameter which is perpendicular to the given tangent. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

The centre is C=(6,-a), radius 3\sqrt2. The line is x+y-2a=0. The distance from C to the line is

\frac{|6-a-2a|}{\sqrt2}=\frac{|6-3a|}{\sqrt2}.

Tangency requires this to equal 3\sqrt2:
|6-3a|=6\Longrightarrow |a-2|=2.

Thus \boxed{a=0\text{ or }a=4}.
For the greater value a=4, the centre is (6,-4). The given tangent has gradient -1, so the perpendicular diameter has gradient 1 and passes through the centre:
y+4=x-6.
Therefore \boxed{y=x-10}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.





Question 19 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q8
A circle with equation
x^2+y^2-6x+2y-15=0
meets the y-axis at the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P.
Find the coordinates of (P). [8]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Complete the square:

(x-3)^2+(y+1)^2=25.

On the y-axis, x=0:
y^2+2y-15=0=(y-3)(y+5).

Thus A=(0,3), B=(0,-5).
The centre is (3,-1). At A, the radius gradient is -4/3, so the tangent gradient is 3/4:
y-3=\frac34x.
At B, the radius gradient is 4/3, so the tangent gradient is -3/4:
y+5=-\frac34x.
Solving,
3+\frac34x=-5-\frac34x
\Longrightarrow x=-\frac{16}{3},qquad y=-1.

Therefore \boxed{P=(-16/3,-1)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q8, and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.





Question 20 · 9709/12/O/N/24 Q8(a–b)
The equation of a circle is
x^2+y^2+px+2y+q=0,
where p and q are constants.

Express the equation in the form (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2, where a is to be given in terms of p and r^2 is to be given in terms of p and q. [2]

The line x+2y=10 is the tangent to the circle at A(4,3).


Find the equation of the normal to the circle at A. [3]



Find the values of p and q. [5]



Show detailed mark scheme answer





x^2+px+y^2+2y+q=0

gives

\boxed{\left(x+\frac p2\right)^2+(y+1)^2=\frac{p^2}{4}-q+1}.

Thus the centre is \left(-\frac p2,-1\right).
(b)(i) The tangent x+2y=10 has gradient -\frac12, so the normal has gradient 2. Through A=(4,3),
y-3=2(x-4),
so \boxed{y=2x-5}.
(b)(ii) The centre lies on the normal. Since its y-coordinate is -1,
-1=2x-5\Longrightarrow x=2.
Therefore -\frac p2=2, so p=-4. Substituting A=(4,3) into the original equation,
16+9-16+6+q=0\Longrightarrow q=-15.

Hence \boxed{p=-4,\quad q=-15}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf.

title: 1.3 Coordinate geometry
text:
3. Quick checklist


能由两点求 gradient、midpoint 和 straight-line equation
能写出 perpendicular bisector，并使用 (m_1m_2=-1)
能把 circle equation 化为标准式并读出 centre/radius
能用 radius perpendicular to tangent 求 tangent equation
能用 substitution 和 discriminant 判断 line-circle intersections
能使用 distance from a point to a line 处理 tangent condition

title: 1.5 Trigonometry
text:
重要本节考纲要求



本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.5 Trigonometry：

sketch and use sine、cosine、tangent graphs，角度可用 degrees 或 radians；
使用 30^\circ、45^\circ、60^\circ 及相关角的 exact values；
使用 \sin^{-1}x、\cos^{-1}x、\tan^{-1}x 的 principal values；
使用基本 trigonometric identities，解给定 interval 内的 equations；
识别 y=a\sin(bx)+c、y=a\cos(bx)+c 的 amplitude、period、midline 与 transformations。

下列 16 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干只把 PDF 排版符号整理为 LaTeX，没有改写或编造题目；答案按对应 mark scheme 的得分步骤展开。

title: 1.5 Trigonometry
text:
1. Core knowledge

Exact values and identities
\sin\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac12,\quad\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac12,\quad\sin\frac{\pi}{4}=\cos\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\quad\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\cos\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1,\qquad\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}.
做 identity proof 时先统一分母，再使用 \sin^2x+\cos^2x=1；解 equation 时最后必须按题目 interval 补齐所有 quadrant solutions。


Equations and graphs
若 0\le x\le2\pi，则
\sin x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,\pi-\alpha;\quad\cos x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,2\pi-\alpha;\quad\tan x=a\Rightarrow x=\alpha,\pi+\alpha.
对 y=a\sin(bx)+c 或 y=a\cos(bx)+c：
\text{amplitude}=|a|,\qquad\text{period}=\frac{2\pi}{|b|},\qquad\text{midline }y=c.


Ratios, exact values and identities
在 right triangle 中

\sin\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}},\qquad
\cos\theta=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}},\qquad
\tan\theta=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}.

除 30^\circ、45^\circ、60^\circ 外，要熟悉相关的 negative-angle、supplementary-angle 和 quadrant signs。基本恒等式为
\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1,
并可由此得到 1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta（在使用 sec notation 的题目中）。证明 identity 时通常先把所有 terms 写成 \sin、\cos，再统一分母或使用 \sin^2+\cos^2=1。


Solving trigonometric equations
先 isolate 一个 trig ratio，再求 principal angle。对 0\le\theta\le2\pi：

\sin\theta=a\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha,\pi-\alpha;\quad
\cos\theta=a\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha,2\pi-\alpha;\quad
\tan\theta=a\Rightarrow\theta=\alpha,\pi+\alpha.

若方程含有 \sin^2\theta、\cos^2\theta 或同时含 \sin\theta,\cos\theta，可先用 identity 或乘以 \sin\theta / \cos\theta 化成 quadratic；factorise 后必须检查每个 root 是否在 [-1,1] 以及是否满足原方程的 denominator restrictions。


Graph features and inverse trig
对 y=a\sin(bx)+c、y=a\cos(bx)+c，|a| 是 amplitude，2\pi/|b| 是 period，y=c 是 midline；a<0 会产生 reflection in the x-axis。Tangent graph 的 period 是 \pi，并有 vertical asymptotes。
\sin^{-1}、\cos^{-1}、\tan^{-1} 表示 inverse functions 的 principal values，不是 reciprocal。最后答案必须统一成题目要求的 degrees 或 radians，并列出指定 interval 内的全部 solutions。

title: 1.5 Trigonometry
text:
2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions


Question 1 · 9709/11/M/J/20 Q7(a–b)

Prove \frac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\frac2{\cos\theta}.
Hence solve the equation when the right-hand side is 3/\sin\theta, for 0\le\theta\le2\pi. [3+3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{(1+\sin\theta)^2+\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\frac{2+2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\boxed{\frac2{\cos\theta}}.
Then 2/\cos\theta=3/\sin\theta, so \tan\theta=3/2. Therefore
\boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}\frac32,\ \pi+\tan^{-1}\frac32=0.983,\ 4.12\text{ rad}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-11.pdf.





Question 2 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q2(a–b)
Express 3\cos\theta=8\tan\theta as a quadratic in \sin\theta. Hence find the acute angle in degrees. [3+2]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos\theta and using \cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta:
3(1-\sin^2\theta)=8\sin\theta\Longrightarrow\boxed{3\sin^2\theta+8\sin\theta-3=0}.
Thus (3\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+3)=0. Only \sin\theta=1/3 is possible, so
\boxed{\theta=\sin^{-1}\frac13=19.5^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q2(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.





Question 3 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q9(a–c)
f(x)=2-3\sin2x,\qquad g(x)=-2f(x),\qquad0\le x\le\pi.
State the ranges of f and g. [3]

Sketch, on the given diagram, the graph of y=g(x).
Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the curve y=f(x) on to y=h(x), where


h(x)=g(x+\pi),\qquad -\pi\le x\le0.

[2+3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Because 2x covers a complete cycle, -1\le\sin2x\le1. Hence
\boxed{-1\le f(x)\le5}.
Multiplying the range by -2 reverses the endpoints:
\boxed{-10\le g(x)\le2}.

Since g=-2f, the graph has the same x-coordinates as f, with all y-coordinates multiplied by -2. It passes through (0,-4), (\pi/4,2), (3\pi/4,-10) and (\pi,-4).
Since f(x+\pi)=f(x),


h(x)=-2f(x+\pi).

Thus translate the graph \pi units to the left, reflect it in the x-axis, and stretch it parallel to the y-axis by scale factor 2.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q9(a–c), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.





Question 4 · 9709/11/O/N/20 Q7(a–b)

Show \frac{\sin\theta}{1-\sin\theta}-\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=2\tan^2\theta.
Hence solve the equation when the left-hand side is 8, for 0<\theta<\pi. [3+3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}=\frac{2\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\boxed{2\tan^2\theta}.
So 2\tan^2\theta=8, giving \tan\theta=\pm2. The two solutions in (0,\pi) are
\boxed{\theta=\tan^{-1}2,\ \pi-\tan^{-1}2=1.107,\ 2.034\text{ rad}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709_w20_qp_11.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w20_ms_11.pdf.





Question 5 · 9709/13/M/J/21 Q4(a–b)
Show \frac{\tan x+\sin x}{\tan x-\sin x}=k may be expressed as \frac{1+\cos x}{1-\cos x}=k. Hence express \cos x in terms of k. [2+2]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Using \tan x=\sin x/\cos x,
\frac{\tan x+\sin x}{\tan x-\sin x}=\frac{\sin x(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1-\cos x)}=\boxed{\frac{1+\cos x}{1-\cos x}}.
Rearrange:
1+\cos x=k(1-\cos x)\Longrightarrow\boxed{\cos x=\frac{k-1}{k+1}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_s21_qp_13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching 9709_s21_ms_13.pdf.





Question 6 · 9709/11/O/N/21 Q3
Solve by factorising:
6\cos\theta\tan\theta-3\cos\theta+4\tan\theta-2=0,\qquad0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

3\cos\theta(2\tan\theta-1)+2(2\tan\theta-1)=0,
so (2\tan\theta-1)(3\cos\theta+2)=0. Therefore \tan\theta=1/2 or \cos\theta=-2/3:
\boxed{\theta=26.6^\circ\text{ or }131.8^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_11.pdf, Q3, and matching 9709_w21_ms_11.pdf.





Question 7 · 9709/12/O/N/21 Q1
Solve 2\cos\theta=7-\frac3{\cos\theta} for -90^\circ<\theta<90^\circ. [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos\theta:
2\cos^2\theta-7\cos\theta+3=0=(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta-3).
The root \cos\theta=3 is impossible. Thus \cos\theta=1/2, and the symmetric interval gives
\boxed{\theta=-60^\circ\text{ or }60^\circ}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_w21_ms_12.pdf.





Question 8 · 9709/13/O/N/21 Q7(a–b)
Show that \frac{\tan x+\cos x}{\tan x-\cos x}=k becomes (k+1)\sin^2x+(k-1)\sin x-(k+1)=0. Hence solve the original equation for k=4, 0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ. [4+4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos x and using \cos^2x=1-\sin^2x gives
\boxed{(k+1)\sin^2x+(k-1)\sin x-(k+1)=0}.
For k=4:
5\sin^2x+3\sin x-5=0,\qquad\sin x=\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{109}}{10}.
Only the positive root is admissible, so
\boxed{x=48.1^\circ\text{ or }131.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_w21_qp_13.pdf, Q7(a–b), and matching 9709_w21_ms_13.pdf.





Question 9 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q1
Solve 4\sin\theta+\tan\theta=0 for 0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ. [3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

\sin\theta\left(4+\frac1{\cos\theta}\right)=0.
The endpoints are excluded, so \sin\theta\ne0. Therefore \cos\theta=-1/4, and the second-quadrant solution is
\boxed{\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac14\right)=104.5^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q1, and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 10 · 9709/12/M/J/23 Q7(a)(i–ii)

By expanding (\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2, find the three solutions of (\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2=1 for 0\le\theta\le\pi.
Hence verify that the only solutions of \cos\theta+\sin\theta=1 are 0 and \frac12\pi. [3+2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer


(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2=1+\sin2\theta.

Thus \sin2\theta=0, giving
\boxed{\theta=0,\frac{\pi}{2},\pi}.
Substitution into the unsquared equation gives 1,1,-1 respectively, so
\boxed{\theta=0\text{ and }\frac{\pi}{2}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_s23_qp_12.pdf, Q7(a)(i–ii), and matching 9709_s23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 11 · 9709/12/O/N/23 Q5(a–b)
The first, second and third terms of a geometric progression are \sin\theta, \cos\theta and 2-\sin\theta, where \theta radians is acute. Find \theta. [3]

Using this value of \theta, find the sum of the first 10 terms of the progression. Give the answer in the form \dfrac{b}{\sqrt{c}-1}, where b and c are integers to be found. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

The GP condition is \cos^2\theta=\sin\theta(2-\sin\theta). Since \cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta,
1-\sin^2\theta=2\sin\theta-\sin^2\theta\Longrightarrow\sin\theta=\frac12.
Acuteness selects
\boxed{\theta=\frac{\pi}{6}}.

The common ratio is


r=\frac{\cos(\pi/6)}{\sin(\pi/6)}=\sqrt3.

Therefore

S_{10}=\frac{\frac12\left((\sqrt3)^{10}-1\right)}{\sqrt3-1}
=\boxed{\frac{121}{\sqrt3-1}},
 so b=121 and c=3.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching 9709_w23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 12 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q5(a–b)

Prove \frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{1+\cos x}=-\cos x.
Hence solve \frac{\sin^2x-\cos x-1}{2+2\cos x}=\frac14 for 0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ. [3+3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

\sin^2x-\cos x-1=1-\cos^2x-\cos x-1=-\cos x(1+\cos x),
which proves (a). In (b), the denominator is doubled, so the left side is -\frac12\cos x. Hence \cos x=-1/2 and
\boxed{x=120^\circ\text{ or }240^\circ}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.





Question 13 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q3(a–b)

Show that \frac{7\tan\theta}{\cos\theta}+12=0 becomes 12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0.
Hence solve the original equation for 0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ. [3+3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

Multiplying by \cos^2\theta gives 7\sin\theta+12\cos^2\theta=0. Replacing \cos^2\theta by 1-\sin^2\theta gives
\boxed{12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0}.
The factors are (3\sin\theta+4)(4\sin\theta-3), so \sin\theta=3/4. Therefore
\boxed{\theta=48.6^\circ\text{ or }131.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.





Question 14 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q4(a–b)

Show that \cos x(7\tan x-5\cos x)=1 can be written as a\sin^2x+b\sin x+c=0.
Hence solve it for 0^\circ<x<180^\circ. [3+3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

7\sin x-5\cos^2x=1\Longrightarrow7\sin x-5(1-\sin^2x)=1,
so
5\sin^2x+7\sin x-6=0=(5\sin x-3)(\sin x+2).
Only \sin x=3/5 is valid. Hence
\boxed{x=\sin^{-1}\frac35=36.9^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.





Question 15 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q8(a–b)

\beta is between 90^\circ and 180^\circ and \sin\beta=a. Express \tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta in terms of a.
Solve \sin^2\theta+2\cos^2\theta=4\sin\theta+3 for 0^\circ<\theta<360^\circ. [3+5]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

In quadrant II, \cos\beta=-\sqrt{1-a^2}. Thus
\boxed{\tan^2\beta-3\sin\beta\cos\beta=\frac{a^2}{1-a^2}+3a\sqrt{1-a^2}}.
For (b), use \cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta:
\sin^2\theta+2(1-\sin^2\theta)=4\sin\theta+3\Longrightarrow\sin^2\theta+4\sin\theta+1=0.
The valid root is \sin\theta=-2+\sqrt3, giving
\boxed{\theta=195.6^\circ\text{ or }344.4^\circ\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q8(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.





Question 16 · 9709/13/O/N/24 Q4
Solve 4\sin^4\theta+12\sin^2\theta-7=0 for 0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ. [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Let u=\sin^2\theta. Then 4u^2+12u-7=0, so
u=\frac{-12\pm16}{8}=1/2\text{ or }-3.
Reject u=-3. Hence \sin^2\theta=1/2, and
\boxed{\theta=45^\circ,\ 135^\circ,\ 225^\circ,\ 315^\circ}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q4, and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p13.pdf.

title: 1.7 Differentiation
text:
重要本节考纲要求



本页依据 9709 Mathematics 2026–2027 syllabus 1.7 Differentiation：

理解 gradient、first derivative 和 second derivative；
对 rational powers 使用 power rule、constant multiples、sums、differences 和 chain rule；
应用 differentiation 求 gradients、tangents、normals、increasing/decreasing intervals 和 rates of change；
找 stationary points，并用 second derivative 判断 maximum 或 minimum。

下列 15 组题目均来自工作区保存的 Paper 1 原始 past-paper PDF。题干只把 PDF 排版符号整理为 LaTeX，没有改写或编造题目；答案按对应 mark scheme 的得分步骤展开。

title: 1.7 Differentiation
text:
1. Core knowledge

Basic rules
\frac{d}{dx}(x^n)=nx^{n-1},\qquad\frac{d}{dx}(cf)=c\frac{df}{dx},\qquad\frac{d}{dx}(f\pm g)=f'\pm g'.
若 y=f(g(x))，chain rule 为
\frac{dy}{dx}=f'(g(x))g'(x).
Stationary point 满足 dy/dx=0。若 d^2y/dx^2>0 是 minimum，若 d^2y/dx^2<0 是 maximum。


Tangent, normal and rates
点 (x_0,y_0) 处 tangent 的 gradient 是 f'(x_0)：
y-y_0=f'(x_0)(x-x_0).
若 tangent gradient 为 m，normal gradient 为 -1/m。Connected rates of change 使用 chain rule：
\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}.
做 rates 题时先在指定点求 dy/dx，再代入已知 rate；单位要跟题目保持一致。


Differentiation from first principles
Derivative 的定义是

f'(x)=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}.

它表示 graph 在该点的 instantaneous gradient。对 composite power function，令 u=ax+b 或 u=f(x)，则

\frac{d}{dx}(ax+b)^n=an(ax+b)^{n-1},\qquad
\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)]^n=n[f(x)]^{n-1}f'(x).

遇到 fractional powers，先写成 index form，再使用 power rule 和 chain rule。


Increasing, decreasing and stationary points
在指定 domain 内，dy/dx>0 表示 curve increasing，dy/dx<0 表示 decreasing。Stationary point 由
\frac{dy}{dx}=0
得到；再代回原方程求 coordinates。用 second derivative：d^2y/dx^2>0 为 local minimum，d^2y/dx^2<0 为 local maximum；若 second derivative 等于 0，则必须进一步检查 gradient sign 或其他信息。
在 tangent/normal 题中，先求 tangent gradient m=dy/dx，再使用 normal gradient -1/m；vertical tangent 或 horizontal tangent 时要单独处理。


Connected rates of change
若变量都随时间变化，使用

\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt},\qquad
\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\frac{dr}{dt}.

先写出变量之间的 geometric relationship，再对时间 t differentiation，最后只在同一个指定时刻代入数值，并检查 rate 的 units。

title: 1.7 Differentiation
text:
2. Verified Paper 1 past-paper questions


Question 1 · 9709/11/M/J/20 Q5(a–b)
The line y=mx+c is tangent to the curve xy=16. (a) Express m in terms of c. (b) Given m=-4, find the set of values of c for which the line intersects the curve at two distinct points.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Write the curve as y=16/x. Its gradient is
\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{16}{x^2}.
At the contact point x=t, tangent gradient m=-16/t^2, while the tangent intercept is
c=\frac{16}{t}-mt=\frac{16}{t}+\frac{16}{t}=\frac{32}{t}.
Thus t=32/c and
\boxed{m=-\frac{c^2}{64}}.
For m=-4, intersections satisfy
-4x+\!c=\frac{16}{x}\Longrightarrow4x^2-cx+16=0.
Two distinct real roots require c^2-256>0, hence
\boxed{c<-16\text{ or }c>16}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-11.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-11.pdf.





Question 2 · 9709/11/M/J/20 Q8(a)
The curve is y=\frac8{x+2} and the line is 2y+x=8. They intersect at A and B. Point C lies on the curve and the tangent at C is parallel to AB. Find the coordinates of A,B,C. [6]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

The line is y=4-\frac x2. Equating with the curve:
\frac8{x+2}=4-\frac x2\Longrightarrow x(x-6)=0.
Thus A=(0,4) and B=(6,1). The gradient of AB is -1/2. Since
\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac8{(x+2)^2},

the tangent at C is parallel to AB when
-\frac8{(x+2)^2}=-\frac12\Longrightarrow(x+2)^2=16.
The point shown on the relevant branch is x=2, giving y=2. Hence
\boxed{A=(0,4),\quad B=(6,1),\quad C=(2,2)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-11.pdf, Q8(a), and matching 9709-s20-ms-11.pdf.





Question 3 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q3(a–b)
A spherical weather balloon is inflated at a constant volume rate of 600 cm^3 per second. (a) Find its radius after 30 seconds. (b) Find the rate of increase of the radius after 30 seconds.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

After 30 seconds, V=18000. Since V=\frac43\pi r^3,
r^3=\frac{3(18000)}{4\pi}=\frac{13500}{\pi},\qquad\boxed{r=16.3\text{ cm (3 s.f.)}}.
Differentiate with respect to time:
\frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}.
At 30 seconds,
\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{600}{4\pi r^2}=0.1806\ldots.
Therefore
\boxed{\frac{dr}{dt}=0.181\text{ cm s}^{-1}\text{ (3 s.f.)}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.





Question 4 · 9709/12/M/J/20 Q6(a–b)
The curve is y=2x^2+kx+k-1. (a) Given that y=2x+3 is tangent to the curve, find k. (b) Given k=2, express the curve in completed-square form and state the vertex.


Show detailed mark scheme answer


At an intersection,

2x^2+kx+k-1=2x+3\Longrightarrow2x^2+(k-2)x+k-4=0.
Tangency means discriminant zero:

(k-2)^2-8(k-4)=0
\Longrightarrow k^2-12k+36=0
\Longrightarrow\boxed{k=6}.


With k=2,

y=2x^2+2x+1=2\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\frac12.
Therefore
\boxed{\text{vertex}=\left(-\frac12,\frac12\right)}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-12.pdf, Q6(a–b), and matching 9709-s20-ms-12.pdf.





Question 5 · 9709/13/M/J/20 Q6(a)
A point moves along y=(5x-1)^{1/2} with dx/dt=1/2 units per minute. Find the rate at which y is increasing when x=1. [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

y=(5x-1)^{1/2}\Longrightarrow\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac5{2(5x-1)^{1/2}}.
At x=1,
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac54.
Using \frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt},
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac54\cdot\frac12=\frac58\text{ units per minute}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2020/2020/9709-s20-qp-13.pdf, Q6(a), and matching 9709-s20-ms-13.pdf.





Question 6 · 9709/12/F/M/21 Q6
A curve has \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac6{(3x-2)^3} and passes through A(1,-3). At A, the y-coordinate is increasing at 3 units per second. Find the rate of increase of the x-coordinate. [3]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

At x=1,
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac6{(3-2)^3}=6.
Therefore
\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{dy}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}
\Longrightarrow3=6\frac{dx}{dt}.
Hence
\boxed{\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac12\text{ units per second}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2021/2021/9709_m21_qp_12.pdf, Q6, and matching 9709_m21_ms_12.pdf.





Question 7 · 9709/12/F/M/22 Q11(a–b)
A curve has equation y=\frac{k}{3x-k}+3x, where k is a constant. Find, in terms of k, the values of x at which there is a stationary point. [4]

The function f has a stationary value at x=a and is defined by f(x)=4(3x-4)^{-1}+3x for x\ge\frac32. Find the value of a and determine the nature of the stationary value. [3]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{3k}{(3x-k)^2}+3.
Set this equal to zero:
-\frac{3k}{(3x-k)^2}+3=0
\Longrightarrow(3x-k)^2=k.
Thus
3x-k=\pm\sqrt{k}
\Longrightarrow\boxed{x=\frac{k+\sqrt{k}}3\text{ or }x=\frac{k-\sqrt{k}}3}.

Here k=4, so the possible stationary x-values are 2/3 and 2. The domain x\ge3/2 selects a=2. Also


f''(x)=\frac{72}{(3x-4)^3},

so f''(2)>0. Therefore

\boxed{a=2\text{ and the stationary value is a minimum}.}


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_m22_qp_12.pdf, Q11(a–b), and matching 9709_m22_ms_12.pdf.





Question 8 · 9709/13/O/N/22 Q4
The water volume is V=243-\frac13(9-x)^3 m^3, where x is depth in metres. Water is pumped in at 3.6 m^3 per hour. Find the rate of increase of depth when x=4, in cm per minute.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

Differentiate:
\frac{dV}{dx}=(9-x)^2.
At x=4, dV/dx=25. Thus
\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}
\Longrightarrow3.6=25\frac{dx}{dt}.
So dx/dt=0.144 m h^{-1}. Convert units:
0.144\text{ m h}^{-1}=\frac{14.4}{60}\text{ cm min}^{-1}.
Therefore
\boxed{\frac{dx}{dt}=0.24\text{ cm min}^{-1}}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2022/2022/9709_w22_qp_13.pdf, Q4, and matching 9709_w22_ms_13.pdf.





Question 9 · 9709/12/F/M/23 Q10(a–b)
At (4,-1), the gradient is -3/2. It is given that \frac{dy}{dx}=x^{-1/2}+k. (a) Show k=-2. (b) Find the equation of the curve.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

At x=4,
-\frac32=4^{-1/2}+k=\frac12+k\Longrightarrow\boxed{k=-2}.
Integrate:
y=\int(x^{-1/2}-2)\,dx=2x^{1/2}-2x+C.
Use (4,-1):
-1=2(2)-8+C\Longrightarrow C=3.
Hence
\boxed{y=2\sqrt{x}-2x+3}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_m23_qp_12.pdf, Q10(a–b), and matching 9709_m23_ms_12.pdf.





Question 10 · 9709/11/O/N/23 Q10(a–d)
A curve has a stationary point at (2,-10) and \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6x.

Find dy/dx. [3]
Find the equation of the curve. [3]
Find the coordinates of the other stationary point and determine its nature. [3]
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where it crosses the y-axis. [2]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

Integrate the second derivative:
\frac{dy}{dx}=3x^2+C.
At the stationary point x=2, dy/dx=0:
0=3(2)^2+C\Longrightarrow C=-12.
Therefore
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dx}=3x^2-12}.

Integrating,

y=x^3-12x+C.
Using (2,-10) gives C=6, so \boxed{y=x^3-12x+6}.

Stationary points satisfy 3x^2-12=0, so x=\pm2. At x=-2, y=22. Since d^2y/dx^2=6x<0 there,

\boxed{(-2,22)\text{, a maximum point}}.

At the y-axis, (x,y)=(0,6) and the gradient is -12. Hence the tangent is

\boxed{y=-12x+6}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2023/2023/9709_w23_qp_11.pdf, Q10(a–d), and matching 9709_w23_ms_11.pdf.





Question 11 · 9709/12/M/J/24 Q6(a–b)
The curve is y=2x-8x^{1/2}. It has a minimum point A and intersects the positive x-axis at B. Find the coordinates of A and B. [4]

Find the area of the shaded region between the curve and the line y=\frac{2x-32}{3}. [5]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{dy}{dx}=2-4x^{-1/2}.
At a stationary point,
2-\frac4{\sqrt{x}}=0\Longrightarrow\sqrt{x}=2\Longrightarrow x=4.
Then y=8-16=-8, so A=(4,-8). For the positive intercept,
2x-8\sqrt{x}=0\Longrightarrow\sqrt{x}(2\sqrt{x}-8)=0,
giving x=16. Therefore
\boxed{A=(4,-8),\qquad B=(16,0)}.

The curve and line meet at x=4 and x=16. Between them the curve is above the line, so


\begin{aligned}
\text{area}&=\int_4^{16}\left[2x-8\sqrt{x}-\frac{2x-32}{3}\right]dx\\
&=\boxed{\frac{32}{3}}.
\end{aligned}


 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q6(a–b), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p12.pdf.





Question 13 · 9709/13/M/J/24 Q5(a–c)
The curve is y=2x^2-\frac5{2x}+3. (a) Find the stationary point. (b) Determine its nature. (c) For positive x, determine whether the curve is increasing, decreasing or neither.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{dy}{dx}=4x+\frac5{2x^2}.
Set equal to zero:
8x^3+5=0\Longrightarrow x=-\frac{\sqrt[3]{5}}2.
At this value, with x^3=-5/8, the y-coordinate is
2x^2-\frac5{2x}+3=3+\frac32\sqrt[3]{25}.
Also
\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=4-\frac5{x^3}=12>0
at the stationary point. Hence
\boxed{\left(-\frac{\sqrt[3]{5}}2,\ 3+\frac32\sqrt[3]{25}\right)\text{ is a minimum}}.
For x>0, both terms in dy/dx=4x+5/(2x^2) are positive, so the curve is
\boxed{\text{increasing for all }x>0}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf, Q5(a–c), and matching ms-202406-mathematics-p13.pdf.





Question 14 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q2
The curve y=x^2-\frac ax has a stationary point at (-3,b). Find a and b. [4]


Show detailed mark scheme answer

\frac{dy}{dx}=2x+\frac a{x^2}.
At x=-3,
0=-6+\frac a9\Longrightarrow a=54.
Then
b=(-3)^2-\frac{54}{-3}=9+18=27.
Therefore
\boxed{a=54,\qquad b=27}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q2, and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.





Question 15 · 9709/11/O/N/24 Q5(a–b)
The derivative of a curve is \frac{dy}{dx}=4x-3\sqrt{x}+1.

Find the x-coordinate of the point on the curve at which the gradient is 11/2. [3]
Given that the curve passes through (4,11), find the equation of the curve. [4]



Show detailed mark scheme answer

Set the derivative equal to the required gradient:
4x-3\sqrt{x}+1=\frac{11}{2}.
Let u=\sqrt{x}. Then x=u^2 and
8u^2-6u-9=0=(4u+3)(2u-3).
Since u\ge0, u=3/2. Hence
\boxed{x=\left(\frac32\right)^2=\frac94}.

Integrating,


y=2x^2-2x^{3/2}+x+C.

Using (4,11) gives C=-9, so
\boxed{y=2x^2-2x^{3/2}+x-9}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf, Q5(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p11.pdf.





Question 16 · 9709/12/O/N/24 Q3(a–b)
The curve is y=2x^2-3. Points A and B have x-coordinates 2 and 2+h. (a) Find the gradient of chord AB in terms of h. (b) Explain how the gradient at A follows from your answer.


Show detailed mark scheme answer

y_A=2(2)^2-3=5,\qquad y_B=2(2+h)^2-3.
The chord gradient is

\frac{y_B-y_A}{(2+h)-2}
=\frac{2(2+h)^2-3-5}{h}
=\boxed{8+2h}.

As h\to0, the second point approaches A, so the chord gradient tends to the tangent gradient:
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dx}\bigg|_{x=2}=8}.

 Completed

Source: PastPaper/2024/2024/qp-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf, Q3(a–b), and matching ms-202410-mathematics-p12.pdf.
